profile.summary: hEVO-base-o is the smaller of the two public checkpoints of hEvo, a DNA language model family from MulinLab trained on haplotype sequences from human populations. It reads a DNA sequence of up to 1,024 nucleotides and returns one 768-dimensional vector per nucleotide, plus masked-base predictions that can score a single-nucleotide variant as a log-likelihood ratio of the alternative against the reference allele. The -o checkpoints were trained on public 1000 Genomes Project and HGDP data.

summary_quotes.text: is the base checkpoint in the hEvo public-data model family. It is a bidirectional BERT-style masked language model with one token per nucleotide and a maximum context of 1,024 nucleotides.
uses population-scale haplotype sequence variation to learn DNA representations for variant-effect scoring, regulatory annotation, and population-genetic analysis
Use the final-layer nucleotide representations for downstream analyses, or score a single-nucleotide change from masked-base logits.
The Hugging Face `-o` models were independently pretrained on public **1000 Genomes Project and HGDP** sequences, without target benchmark-label supervision.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: hEVO-base-o is a bidirectional BERT-style masked language model with 12 transformer layers and hidden size 768, and one token per nucleotide with no boundary tokens. The family README describes two training stages: span-masked representation learning on deduplicated haplotype windows, then calibration of the nucleotide prediction head on variant-centred contexts. To score a single-nucleotide variant, the variant site is masked once and the alternative-allele logit minus the reference-allele logit at that site gives the log-likelihood ratio. The weight file also holds tensors for an optional frequency branch, which is off by default and not built when loading.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: This checkpoint is the public-data base model of the hEvo family; its sibling is hEVO-large-o. The README says its file hash matches the hEvo-open-base weights evaluated in the authors' benchmarks. The card's example pins revision fa6139047c21d92b58bd8eda49ea2f89a884e33c for the weights and custom code, while the card text is maintained on main. The examples were tested with PyTorch 2.6.0 and Transformers 4.57.1. A result should name hEVO-base-o and the revision used.

steps.title: Load the model and embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import torch
from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

REPO = "MulinLab/hEVO-base-o"
# Freeze the checkpoint and its custom code for reproducible inference.
REVISION = "fa6139047c21d92b58bd8eda49ea2f89a884e33c"
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

load_options = dict(revision=REVISION, token=True, trust_remote_code=True)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(REPO, **load_options)
config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
    REPO,
    use_frequency_embedding=False,
    use_flash_attention=False,
    **load_options,
)
assert config.use_frequency_embedding is False
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(
    REPO,
    config=config,
    attn_implementation="eager",
    dtype=torch.float32,
    **load_options,
).to(device).eval()

def encode_dna(sequence):
    sequence = sequence.strip().upper()
    if not 0 < len(sequence) <= config.max_position_embeddings:
        raise ValueError("Provide a sequence of 1 to 1,024 nucleotides.")
    if set(sequence) - set("ACGTN"):
        raise ValueError("DNA must contain only A, C, G, T or N.")
    encoded = tokenizer(sequence, return_tensors="pt", truncation=False)
    # This custom tokenizer returns 1D tensors for a single sequence.
    encoded = {
        key: value.unsqueeze(0) if value.ndim == 1 else value
        for key, value in encoded.items()
    }
    if "attention_mask" not in encoded:
        encoded["attention_mask"] = torch.ones_like(encoded["input_ids"])
    return {key: value.to(device) for key, value in encoded.items()}

sequence = "ACGTTGCATGTCGCATGATGCATGAGAGCT"
inputs = encode_dna(sequence)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(**inputs, output_hidden_states=True, return_dict=True)
    token_embeddings = outputs.hidden_states[-1]  # [batch, length, hidden_size]

    # Optional: summarize the last-layer nucleotide embeddings by mean pooling.
    keep = inputs["attention_mask"].unsqueeze(-1).to(token_embeddings.dtype)
    sequence_embedding = (token_embeddings * keep).sum(dim=1) / keep.sum(
        dim=1
    ).clamp_min(1)

print("Last-layer token embeddings:", tuple(token_embeddings.shape))
print("Mean-pooled sequence embedding:", tuple(sequence_embedding.shape))
EOF
